idea: Send a travelling wave through the drawing while keeping Wavelength fixed.
note: Phase is in radians: one cycle is 0–2π. A good first 24-frame experiment.

idea: Build an appear–hold–disappear movement, for example on Carve’s endpoint.
note: Check speed at the seam as well as matching values. A cosine is simpler for gentle breathing.

idea: Grow the structure piece by piece, then retrace the growth backwards.
note: Keep the module and Seed fixed. Use half the loop forwards and half backwards without duplicating endpoint frames.

idea: Align the source drawing before animating it.
note: Recentering each frame’s changing bounds can cancel the intended movement or shift the whole picture.

idea: Use a small Tilt change to sway the antenna booms.
note: Proposed: Wind phase and amplitude acting on the same masts and cables. Keep mast count and Seed fixed.

idea: Let a Single form breathe; Rolls can suggest a slowly moving body.
note: Start with one form. Field placement and occlusion can change. Proposed: fixed placement and a shared Body phase.

idea: Open and close the gaps between copies, or spread them into a fan.
note: Keep Copies fixed. Allow enough space for the outermost copies to stay on the page.

idea: Provide a shared base value to which Math adds the loop movement.
note: Value is not a clock. Use Frame or LFO to supply changing values.

idea: Turn a light character field dense and back, or convert an animated drawing to ASCII.
note: Keep Columns and the grid fixed. Character changes are discrete; 24 frames suit an intentionally stepped effect.

idea: Rotate the existing asteroid field with Rotate.
note: Proposed: persistent asteroid identities, orbital paths, spin phase and a closed ship route. Changing Seed makes the field flicker.

idea: Use a small parameter cycle to reshape a chaotic drawing and return it to its start.
note: Adjacent frames can differ dramatically; automatic fitting may change scale. Start with a small range. A fixed camera would help.

idea: Move a fixed barcode back and forth behind a Crop window.
note: Proposed: individual bar heights and phases with a fixed bar count. Width and spacing can change which bars fit at the end.

idea: Move a line marker along a fixed belt to make its mechanism readable.
note: Proposed: Belt phase, moving markers and pulley spoke angles. The existing Loop setting means a closed belt, not an animation loop.

idea: Bring Magnet poles together and apart, or breathe the fold depth in Drape or Pleat.
note: Keep mode and line density fixed. Clipping may split strokes. Proposed: a separate Noise or Flow phase for each mode.

idea: Quantise the drawing into angular steps and restore it.
note: This is deliberately stepped. Keep Sample rate fixed to distinguish snapping from resampling changes.

idea: In Manual mode, move or resize one metaball within the soft volume.
note: Keep ball count and mesh resolution fixed. Plot the paths output or use Mesh Slice. Watch the node’s automatic fitting.

idea: Stretch and tilt the same ring forms in turn.
note: Placement collisions and changing ring counts can cause jumps. Proposed: frozen centres and persistent ring identities.

idea: Sway a finished blueberry sprig with Lens, Wave or Rotate.
note: Proposed: branch-specific wind phases and swinging berries. Do not alternate leaf and berry choices each frame.

idea: Breathe the dots in place, or slide the entire line of text.
note: Keep text and character positions fixed. This art experiment is not a Braille legibility test; punching holes is unnecessary.

idea: Grow connections between fixed points and retract them.
note: Lock the points and Rule. Moving points can change K-nearest or Delaunay connections; Source order is more predictable.

idea: Shorten and shift the same grid lines to open and close the surface.
note: Keep Cell, Density and Seed fixed. Threshold changes make lines appear or disappear in steps.

idea: Move a brush-pressure wave along the same line.
note: Requires supported Z pressure and a tested physical range. SVG/DXF does not carry this pressure motion; use real line geometry for an ordinary pen.

idea: Open the seams of a fixed spiky mass and extend its spikes.
note: Proposed: breathing per lobe with fixed centres. Reduce fills for an initial 48-frame test.

idea: Pass the same cable bundle through a Wave modifier.
note: Proposed: a closed noise phase for the guiding field. Waviness changes integrated routes, so a small adjustment need not create a small movement.

idea: Reveal the antenna array with a gentle change in viewing angle.
note: Start with a small Yaw oscillation. Check automatic fitting before trying a complete rotation.

idea: Breathe a cage deformation from zero to maximum and back.
note: Keep Seed and Cage cells fixed. Pin edges preserves the page edges; useful for animating many static generators.

idea: Plot a calibration sheet before a long animation run.
note: Keep dimensions and start/end crosses fixed. Its purpose is to reveal scale and alignment errors, not to animate.

idea: Lay out prepared content on small cards.
note: Use Frame Grid for collecting animation frames. Card Sheet alone does not evaluate different times.

idea: Write a drawing into view, then erase it along the same strokes.
note: End t 0→1 is a one-way reveal. For a loop, use an out-and-back value or a moving window on a closed path; open paths need a deliberate return.

idea: Vary Threshold to make light streaks denser and sparser.
note: Proposed: periodic water-surface phase. Changing Seed does not produce continuous water; contours may still appear and disappear.

idea: Break apart the same tiled drawing and assemble it again.
note: Keep Scale and Seed fixed so the fragments retain their identities.

idea: Rotate chain links in their own planes, changing the over/under relationships.
note: Keep Links and hatch spacing fixed. Inspect moving occlusion boundaries; 48 frames suit a full turn better.

idea: Reveal a fixed chip drawing with Carve or a moving Crop window.
note: Proposed: pulses along conductors and block-by-block reveal. Animating density rebuilds the structure.

idea: Let fixed fragments travel with an upstream animation.
note: Proposed: Chop offset in millimetres to move gaps and colour divisions along a path. Length changes the number of pieces.

idea: Make a walking or running loop using Animate → Single instant.
note: Check the gait endpoints. Jumps and somersaults are events; give them a return or a rest interval.

idea: Generate a fixed circle packing and deform the finished result.
note: Proposed: vary radii around fixed accepted centres. Min/Max radius or Seed can rebuild the entire packing.

idea: Reveal a fixed conductor network with Carve and retract it.
note: Proposed: a signal pulse travelling by path distance. Keep Blocks, Traces and Seed fixed.

idea: Rotate the clock-face pattern through one full turn.
note: Twelve identical sectors can appear stationary. Distinguish one sector or try a small Keystone oscillation instead.

idea: Float a cloud layer slowly from side to side.
note: Proposed: persistent cloud identities, closed drift paths and breathing lobes. Size changes can alter overlaps and placement.

idea: Separate the coloured registration artwork and bring it together again.
note: Treat this as moving content. Add separate static Reg Marks outside it. Multiple colours increase pen-change work.

idea: Contract and expand the spring wound around a path.
note: Keep Pitch fixed. Proposed: a phase that slides the coils along the host path.

idea: Send a short sequence to separate outputs.
note: The current maximum is 16. For 24–48 frames use Frame Grid Animate, whose Total reaches 64.

idea: Move light around a folded surface and animate its hatch shadows.
note: Keep Facets, Relief and Seed fixed. Shading changes line counts in steps; start with sparse hatching and 48 frames.

idea: Let the same coloured scribble breathe and bend.
note: Keep Bundles, Lines per bundle and Seed fixed. Start with Arcs. Automatic fitting may conceal changes in overall spread.

idea: Bend and extend comet tails together.
note: Keep Count, Tail lines and Seed fixed. A full turn of the light direction needs margin and a check of fitting behaviour.

idea: Use Motion modes such as Wave, Orbit, Row squeeze, Shift and Zoom In & out.
note: Timeline already uses i/N. Shift and Zoom change whole letters; one-way Zoom and Typewriter need a deliberate restart.

idea: In Power z^n mode, bend the grid with a small exponent oscillation.
note: Avoid singular settings. Clipping and subdivision thresholds can flicker; turn labels off for the art experiment.

idea: Move a revealing window, breathe a circle or rotate a triangle.
note: Add registration marks afterwards. In Wired region mode animate the boundary. The Keep menu is not a numeric animation control.

idea: Soften and sharpen a fixed height field with Roughness.
note: Proposed: a periodic height-field coordinate. Varying Seed produces boiling, not a smooth loop; keep it fixed.

idea: Run Game of Life forwards and reverse the same evolution.
note: 24–48 generations rarely form a natural loop. Alternatively find an oscillator whose period divides the frame count.

idea: Grow and tilt motifs placed on persistent points.
note: Keep points, Spacing and Probability fixed. Proposed: a phase delay per instance for travelling motion.

idea: Widen and narrow coral ridges within the same field.
note: Keep Density, Growth and Seed fixed; Growth can trigger expensive simulation. Proposed: periodic field phase with stable connections.

idea: Open and close the same cracks.
note: Keep Flake size, Chips and Seed fixed. Hatch lines may appear in steps; avoid dense black fills in every test frame.

idea: Sweep a rectangular window over a drawing, or expand and contract it.
note: Content outside the window is removed. Add registration marks afterwards and keep the page size fixed.

idea: Reveal cross-stitch text with Carve or Crop.
note: Keep the hole grid fixed. Use Stitches for the artwork; Holes is a production aid, not a required animation layer.

idea: Design a movement by hand with a controller.
note: Proposed: record channels as keyframes, close the loop and interpolate. Live input does not currently guarantee repeatable frame export.

idea: Reveal and remove fixed lines in a repeatable random order.
note: Keep Seed fixed. This is a stepped dissolve; changing Every Nth can replace many paths at once.

idea: Change the drawing machine’s initial phase to reshape its rosette.
note: Keep crank ratios fixed and start with a small Phase range. Non-integer speed ratios or table rotation may not close after 2π.

idea: Reveal a prepared chart with Carve.
note: Proposed: interpolate data keyframes against fixed axes. The current Data text field is not a numeric animation input.

idea: Pass a fixed camouflage pattern through Wave.
note: Proposed: hatch Phase and Angle on persistent regions. Changing Patches or Seed breaks continuity.

idea: Move source points to make the triangulation change its connections.
note: Edge flips are discrete. For smooth stretching, triangulate fixed points first and deform the resulting network afterwards.

idea: Breathe the diagram’s circles while preserving its network.
note: Proposed: signals along arrows. Freeze nodes and routes so changing size does not rebuild connections.

idea: Cycle through die values 1–6 or change them rhythmically.
note: This is a state sequence, not a morph. Pip size can breathe at a fixed value; six states divide 24 and 48 evenly.

idea: Grow a closed line into a coral-like form and shrink it back.
note: Keep the initial seed and forces fixed. Point insertion is discrete; try 48 frames over a limited iteration range.

idea: Use another pen to highlight differences from the original drawing.
note: Exact can classify an entire shifted drawing as new. Distance thresholds can flicker too; this is not a temporal motion tracker.

idea: Use a fixed image to raise and lower features in a line field.
note: Keep the image, sampling and direction fixed. Pair with Grid for a 48-frame photographic relief.

idea: Build up a pendulum trace and retract it.
note: A chaotic trajectory rarely closes. Use a prepared trace with Carve; a moving physical pendulum needs a separately chosen periodic segment.

idea: Tilt a cloth slowly over its hidden supports.
note: Keep Shapes, Count and Density fixed. Height or tension can change the solution; a fixed camera scale would help.

idea: Reveal the radar array’s depth with a small camera sway.
note: Start with Light detail. Dense latticework takes time to plot. Check automatic fitting; a complete turn is unnecessary.

idea: Wind and unwind a sequence of copies.
note: Keep Copies fixed. Canvas center provides a stable pivot; Path centroid may move with an animated source.

idea: Rotate hatching around static gaps, or breathe the clearance around them.
note: Contour mode can change line counts. Keep Spacing fixed for a calmer line field.

idea: Pulse arrowheads or circular caps at the ends of moving lines.
note: Keep Where and Style fixed. A fragmented source can change the number of caps.

idea: Move an empty circle across the drawing, then reveal the same content again.
note: Add registration marks afterwards. Keep the eraser shape fixed and watch page-edge clipping.

idea: Scatter a drawing’s parts and return them to their original positions.
note: Keep Seed fixed and the zone large enough. Animating the zone can abruptly include new pieces.

idea: Breathe the cloth by changing fold depth and sag.
note: Flag does not imply a built-in clock. Proposed: Wave phase travelling through the same weave grid.

idea: Extend and shorten brush fades at the ends of the same paths.
note: Physical Z motion requires a suitable machine. A 2D SVG cannot reproduce the same ink fade; start with a small test.

idea: Distribute a movement to several parameters with different base values.
note: Fan alone does not create a time delay. Use several LFOs with different Phase values, or a future loop controller.

idea: Deform a fixed fingerprint using Cage Warp.
note: Proposed: fixed centres and a periodic field coordinate. Ring gap and Seed rebuild ridges rather than moving the same ridge continuously.

idea: Tilt a fixed shoal using Heading.
note: Proposed: Tail phase, body bending and per-fish delays with persistent identities. Rotating the whole shoal does not itself resemble swimming.

idea: Fit the source drawing before constructing the animation.
note: Current fitting uses each frame’s bounds. Proposed: shared bounds for the whole 24–48-frame sequence or fixed canvas mapping.

idea: Slide the same strips in different directions and reassemble the image.
note: Keep Segments, Width mode and Seed fixed. Check clipping at the edges.

idea: Vary Curl slightly to make the flow pattern move.
note: Paths can change substantially. Proposed: periodic field Phase and persistent starting points, using a closed noise trajectory instead of changing Seed.

idea: Generate the route map once and reveal it with Carve.
note: Proposed: pulses travelling along traces. Flow angle or Swirl can change discrete route choices across the map.

idea: Open and close the FM flower without changing its base frequencies.
note: Keep fc, fm and Rings fixed. Rotation can add another movement, although symmetry may hide it.

idea: Fold the drawing into a window and straighten it again.
note: The fold boundary intentionally reverses direction. Keep Window and sampling fixed; 48 frames make the movement easier to follow.

idea: Breathe and bend a bundle of lines.
note: Repeated offsets can amplify a small change. Keep Count and Step fixed. Proposed: a shared continuous drift phase.

idea: Change a simple ellipse into the original contour and back.
note: Harmonics is rounded to an integer. Proposed: blend the last harmonic continuously so detail emerges smoothly.

idea: Provide a shared clock for a 24–48-frame loop.
note: wave loop and rot ° use i/N; t uses i/(N−1). Proposed: a separate Loop phase output without changing existing ports.

idea: Collect 24 or 48 frames into numbered plotter sheets.
note: Use Animate, Map canvas and Total 24/48. A 4×3 layout needs 2/4 sheets; 3×2 needs 4/8. Set outer ANIMATE Frames to the sheet count. Avoid Fit each.

idea: Split one drawing into reveal stages or moving line windows.
note: It does not evaluate the full graph at new times. Build-up needs a return sequence or an animated Carve to loop.

idea: Sway loose threads around their fixed attachment points.
note: Keep Spacing, Seed and thread choices fixed. Crossings None may change search decisions; Allowed is more predictable over time.

idea: Move or breathe a lens that refracts a line surface.
note: Zone boundaries create intentional jumps. Keep Radius and Zone width fixed to follow the same rings.

idea: Breathe a completed fruit arrangement using Lens.
note: Proposed: fruit rotation and a morph between whole and cut forms with fixed placement. Cut and Kind are discrete choices.

idea: Extend and lower the same hairs.
note: Keep Spacing and Seed fixed. Proposed: shared wind direction and phase; Angle jitter only increases random deviation.

idea: Reveal a galaxy’s depth with a slow camera orbit.
note: Keep Stars, Arm count and Seed fixed. Yaw is a camera change, not internal star orbits. Proposed: Orbital phase; check fitting stability.

idea: Import an earlier drawing as paths and animate them downstream.
note: Keep True scale and the same file. Machine commands are not animation controls; Z data needs a compatible downstream chain.

idea: Open and close the star network by changing its contact angle.
note: Keep Tiling and Cell fixed. Start with a small angle range that preserves valid intersections.

idea: Strengthen and remove the same glitch pattern.
note: Keep Amount, Skip and Seed fixed to preserve the breaks. This is a deliberate distortion, not gentle natural movement.

idea: Raise a corrupted paper surface into depth and lower it again.
note: Keep Bands and Seed fixed. Camera fitting and strip boundaries can produce jumps.

idea: Shift the same woven rows and bring them together again.
note: Keep Pitch, Fray choices and Seed fixed. Leave room for movement because the edges are clipped.

idea: Change symbols in a fixed halftone grid as the tones change.
note: Glyph changes are discrete. Keep Cell, Jitter, Seed and the source image fixed throughout the sequence.

idea: Separate and rotate the same line fragments, then restore them.
note: Keep Grain, Density and Seed fixed. Large Rotation values can make the result hard to read.

idea: Drop grid fragments and lift them back into place.
note: Keep Release, stamp count and Seed fixed. Reverse falling is an intentional out-and-back effect, not a naturally repeating simulation.

idea: Reveal prepared gravity traces with Carve.
note: Pull and Damping change chaotic integration. Proposed: a moving particle following a cached closed trajectory.

idea: Keep the grid fixed and add Wave, Lens or Cage Warp.
note: Do not animate line counts for a smooth loop. A sparse grid is an excellent first plotting test.

idea: Tilt the hairs in each cell as if in the wind.
note: Keep Cell width/height, Lines per cell and Seed fixed. Shared Angle works now; a per-cell Wind phase would be a useful extension.

idea: Grow an organic loop and retract it.
note: Keep forces, Seed and bounds fixed. Simulation cost repeats for each frame; cached growth would improve the workflow.

idea: Reveal a fixed sequence of footprints in order.
note: Proposed: Reveal per footprint and a walking phase. Changing Steps can rebuild the route; revealing a prepared route is steadier.

idea: Rotate the 3D gyroid, or breathe Iso over a small range.
note: Keep Cells, Slices and Detail fixed. Check the seam and hidden-line cuts; start with sparse sections and 48 frames.

idea: Tilt and raise a Fixed angle hair field.
note: Keep Count, Seed and Region fixed. Flow mode would benefit from a separate time-dependent field phase.

idea: Bulge and twist the same thread network.
note: Keep Anchors, Strands and Seed fixed. Start with a few hundred threads; thousands across 48 frames are a large plotting job.

idea: Breathe the dots in the same point texture.
note: Keep Cell, Scale and Seed fixed. Max K is discrete and should stay fixed in a smooth experiment.

idea: Change a precise drawing into a hand-drawn one and back.
note: Keep Seed fixed. Changing source samples can make noise alignment flicker; proposed: a time-based noise phase.

idea: Wave a wrist and open the fingers.
note: Pose is a menu. Proposed: interpolation between anatomical poses and individual finger Curl. Keep hand count and placement fixed.

idea: Breathe the mixture of two pendulum traces.
note: Keep frequencies, Detune, Duration and sampling fixed. Proposed: initial phases that cycle without changing the duration.

idea: Sway the hatch direction within the same closed shape.
note: Line counts and endpoints change. Keep Spacing fixed and inspect a preview; fine hatching can flicker.

idea: Slide text or expand and contract it.
note: Keep the text and line breaks fixed. Concrete Poetry is a better starting point for individual letter motion.

idea: Sway the himmeli like a hanging ornament.
note: Keep Model and Complexity fixed. Use 48 frames and shared camera scale for a full turn; a small sway suits 24 frames.

idea: Compress ring spacing towards the centre and open it again.
note: Keep Rings, Segments and Seed fixed. Proposed: seamless circulation and tile identities; changing arc directions is a separate stepped mode.

idea: Breathe a Rams contour relief, or convert an animated blue Drawing input into dots or blocks.
note: Keep Cell, the image and drawing area fixed. Dots/Squares change fill strokes in steps. Proposed: image-transform phase and per-frame caching.

idea: Separate photographic colour plates and register them again.
note: Keep Cell and angles fixed. Four pens per frame take work. Actual registration marks should remain separate and stationary.

idea: Use a static reference for capture or tracing.
note: Underlay is not exported as drawing paths. Changing its opacity or calibration corners does not create a plotter animation.

idea: Extend and retract the same ink tendrils.
note: Keep Tendrils, Seed and structural choices fixed. Fragment thresholds may flicker; begin with a small range.

idea: Reduce overlapping ink consistently across the sequence.
note: Adaptive Thin decisions can vary between frames. Compare the processed sequence with the original before a long plotting run.

idea: Breathe the wavelength around fixed wave sources.
note: Proposed: Waves Phase and orbiting sources; Terrain needs periodic noise coordinates. Contours may merge or split.

idea: Dilate and contract the pupil while fibres bend around it.
note: Keep Species, Fibres and Seed fixed. Start with 250–400 fibres and an open pupil; plotting a dark pupil 48 times adds work.

idea: Increase a persistent noise deformation from zero and return.
note: Keep Seed, Scale and source sampling fixed. Changing Seed creates deliberate boiling, not continuous motion.

idea: Reduce pen lifts in each frame.
note: Use the same Gap/Angle settings throughout. Nearby endpoint pairings can change; check for visible flicker from new joins.

idea: Move the Julia parameter around a small circle in the complex plane.
note: Use two LFOs a quarter-cycle apart. Keep Zoom, Bands and Iterations fixed. Fractal topology changes are natural and computation can be expensive.

idea: Rotate a sector of a fixed source drawing.
note: Keep Sectors fixed. A single-sector cycle works only if mirroring and source content actually match at the seam.

idea: Rotate any drawing through one complete turn.
note: Use Frame rot °, a fixed pivot and enough corner clearance. Symmetry can make rotation appear stationary or reversed.

idea: Rotate a knot in 3D so its front and back exchange places.
note: Keep knot type, frequencies and strand count fixed. Check hidden-line boundaries; start with 48 frames and sparse lines.

idea: Breathe the curves of a kolam without changing its crossings.
note: Keep grid, Turns, Strands and Seed fixed. Proposed: a marker travelling along a closed strand.

idea: Rotate a fixed lace drawing, or breathe it with Move / Scale.
note: Rings, Sectors and detail choices are discrete. Internal movement needs a phase for individual motifs.

idea: Expand and contract the turned form.
note: Keep Sheds, Rings and Shape fixed. Tilt suggests depth but is not a complete 3D camera orbit.

idea: Move a glass-like bulge across a grid, or breathe it in place.
note: Keep Radius fixed for a moving lens. High Strength can fold lines over one another; start small.

idea: Extend the letters’ 3D sides and change their direction.
note: Keep Text, Font and fill density fixed. Hatch count changes may flicker; Outline is a lighter test mode.

idea: Drive breathing, part of a rotation or periodic noise in another node.
note: Feed it i/N, not the endpoint-inclusive i/(N−1). Sine is smooth; Triangle reverses sharply, while Saw and Square intentionally jump.

idea: Breathe a fixed lichen surface using a downstream deformation.
note: Proposed: persistent colonies and Growth/Flow phase. Density and Seed can replace the entire patch layout.

idea: Open and close line gaps in a fixed region layout.
note: Keep Zones, Pitch and Seed fixed. Verify Phase units and periodicity before using it for a full loop.

idea: Cycle a Lissajous curve into a form that appears spatial.
note: Use Phase 0–2π, integer fx/fy, Damp 0 and fixed Turns. One continuous path makes this a useful first plotter loop.

idea: Let a woven surface sag and straighten, or slide its layers.
note: Keep Density and Seed fixed. Moiré can flicker strongly; test at the intended scan size.

idea: Open and close branch angles within one fixed generation.
note: Keep Preset, Iteration and Seed fixed. Auto-fit may pump the scale. Animating generations is a separate stepped effect.

idea: Move a magnet around a closed path and pull the line field with it.
note: Use phase-shifted LFOs for the two coordinates, with Radius and Strength fixed. A static reference makes the motion clearer.

idea: Move a magnifier, revealing window or wave over a map.
note: Keep imported data and Fit fixed. Add movement downstream; roads and buildings do not contain time information themselves.

idea: Existing patches can still use an animated mask to clip content.
note: Hidden compatibility node. Use Container for new animation work.

idea: Convert phase into an angle or a distance in millimetres.
note: Current recipe: Frame rot ° → Math divide by 36 → Math divide by 10 → LFO t. This gives i/N without a duplicate endpoint.

idea: Rotate a projected knot on the page.
note: Keep fp/fq and Tube fixed. For a real 3D camera movement, use Knot Tube. Gap is not animation speed.

idea: Combine animated drawings with static backgrounds or registration marks.
note: A fixed background still has to be plotted on each physical frame. Preserve pens and drawing order throughout the sequence.

idea: Change the same structural grid from regular to irregular and back.
note: Keep Rows/Cols, diagonals and Seed fixed. Proposed: time-dependent noise phase for travelling movement.

idea: Move a cross-section through a form and back.
note: Frames (ANIMATE) selects layer slices, not a ready-made loop. Single slice with Slice control is stepped; continuous Z position would help.

idea: Merge and separate cell-like forms.
note: Keep Blobs, Seed and resolution fixed. Contours naturally change connections; use 48 frames and a fixed drawing area.

idea: Move a fixed square field in perspective or deform it with a wave.
note: Proposed: Scale phase on persistent squares. Cell, Max size and Density can change packing and line counts.

idea: Place smaller prepared drawings on a sheet.
note: It does not collect different times by itself. Use Frame Grid Animate for an automatic 24–48-frame sequence.

idea: Move a mirror axis slowly to change the symmetry.
note: Keep Mode fixed. Copies may leave the page; use a final Crop and add static marks afterwards.

idea: Use a light fixed grid to help evaluate capture alignment.
note: There is no need to plot dense millimetre paper on every frame. Four edge marks are usually a lighter production aid.

idea: Overlap two discs and move one while keeping the other fixed.
note: Rotating concentric Rings has no visible effect. Use Hatch/Mesh for rotation, or translate the rings. Keep Pitch fixed and test sparsely.

idea: Tilt the crater landscape in 3D.
note: Keep Craters, Size and Seed fixed. Preserve camera and relief scale to avoid unintended breathing.

idea: Use the existing interpolation between two drawings.
note: Layers currently stops at 12 and Sheets runs forwards only. Proposed: continuous Phase, Loop/Ping-pong and fixed correspondence in this same node.

idea: Reveal or deform a fixed mosaic downstream.
note: A changing source region can create new tiles each frame. Proposed: locked tiling and a transform phase for each tile.

idea: Breathe a mountain range’s height or sway its view.
note: Keep Rows, Scale and Seed fixed. Proposed: periodic terrain phase or camera movement over a fixed height field.

idea: Slide, breathe or orbit any drawing.
note: Canvas center or Custom point avoids drift from changing content bounds. Scale Y 0 follows the X scale.

idea: Fly a flock around a closed route while retaining each bird’s identity.
note: Time uses i/N and internal noise is periodic. Try 48 frames, 60–120 birds, short trails and generous margins.

idea: Reveal mushroom gills with a camera sway.
note: Keep Species, Count and Seed fixed. Increase gill spacing for the test and check automatic fitting.

idea: Thicken the same network like living tissue.
note: Keep Strands, connections and Seed fixed. Thickening can concentrate overlapping ink at junctions.

idea: Write a prepared mycelium network into view and retract it with Carve.
note: Branching and Length change how the network grows. Proposed: cached growth history and Reveal preserving the same branches.

idea: Rotate the carbon lattice in 3D.
note: Keep structure, n and length fixed. Front half reduces drawing but changes visible edges. Begin with a sparse Fullerene.

idea: Prepare alignment or production holes for animation sheets.
note: Not the recommended primary technique for a first animation. Physical punching needs an appropriate tool and backing; SVG does not perform a Z plunge.

idea: Move Shape through a fixed Fill to reveal negative space.
note: Keep Clearance and sampling fixed. Clipping can create many short paths and pen lifts.

idea: Bring discs together and apart, changing their woven over/under structure.
note: Keep Count, Radius and Spacing fixed. Occlusion changes are part of the effect; use 48 frames and adequate line spacing.

idea: Let a fishing net sag and straighten.
note: Keep Cell, Pattern, Jitter and Seed fixed. A light choice for a 24-frame breathing loop.

idea: Untangle a network and reverse the process.
note: Keep Nodes, Links and Seed fixed. Simulation is stepped; proposed: interpolation through a cached layout history.

idea: Move or reveal a fixed numeral drawing.
note: Value is text, not a directly animated number input. Proposed: numeric input and digit-morph phase for a counter.

idea: Hide an animated background behind closed foreground shapes.
note: Keep front/back ordering intentional. Inspect clipping boundaries and add registration marks afterwards.

idea: Spread parallel copies apart and return them together.
note: Keep Copies fixed. Large offsets can introduce cusps and cleanup changes; start with a small spacing range.

idea: Move the vanishing point around a small ellipse.
note: Keep Sides, Seed and Glitches fixed. Proposed: Depth phase for continuous inward travel without an end-frame jump.

idea: Breathe the same winding scribble.
note: Keep Strands, Loops and Seed fixed. Proposed: a travelling orbit phase over a fixed time interval, rather than reshaping the full route.

idea: Breathe the central opening and undulate the ring edges.
note: Keep Rings and detail choices fixed. Proposed: a bulge phase travelling along each persistent ring.

idea: Breathe a fixed crease pattern with Lens or Cage Warp.
note: Splits changes the structure. Actual folding needs persistent facets, hinge angles and a Folding phase control.

idea: Move a fold line across an image and restore it.
note: Abrupt reflection across the fold is intentional. Keep the pivot fixed; 48 frames make the fold direction easier to follow.

idea: Thicken and thin a drawing using real outline geometry.
note: Inner and outer edges can meet at large widths. Filling is possible but increases plotting time.

idea: Raise and lower the canopy formed by parallel lines.
note: Keep Spacing, Levels and Seed fixed. Proposed: shared Wind phase without rebuilding the terraces.

idea: Sway a hatch, dash or chevron pattern in the same region.
note: Keep Pattern, Spacing and Seed fixed. Check random motif placement; if necessary clip a fixed fill field with the animated shape.

idea: Reveal prepared circuit-board traces in sequence.
note: Proposed: Trace phase and Pulse length for a travelling signal. Tracks, Chips and Grid are not smooth time controls.

idea: Reveal a Mesh-mode pebble with a slow camera sway.
note: For Spiral shells, prefer Warp or Carve. Keep Mode, Eyes and Turns fixed; check placement and fitting.

idea: Change colour groups rhythmically on the same drawing.
note: Changing Group repartitions paths rather than advancing one palette step. Proposed: integer Palette offset. Consider the number of pen changes.

idea: Reshape a pendulum trace by varying its initial phase.
note: Keep Arms, speeds and duration fixed. Coupling means a 2π loop needs testing; a small out-and-back phase is a safer starting point.

idea: Rotate a perforated form to reveal its rear openings.
note: Keep hole count and Seed fixed. Occlusion and dense lines make this a later 48-frame project rather than a first test.

idea: Sway a corridor’s vanishing point to suggest camera movement.
note: Keep Gap, ledges and doors fixed. Proposed: closed forward camera travel through a repeating corridor.

idea: Create a calibrated source shape from a photo and animate it downstream.
note: Freeze calibration, image and threshold. This is not automatic video segmentation; aligning a captured sequence is a separate step.

idea: Vary the golden angle slightly to open and close spiral families.
note: Keep Count and C fixed. Start with a very small range; outer points move quickly under larger changes and may flicker.

idea: Tilt a field of pins together as if in the wind.
note: Keep Pins, Chaos and Seed fixed. The random layout must remain identical between frames.

idea: Move several grids in depth to create changing moiré.
note: Phase 0–1 turns the camera through 360°; Bob adds periodic tilt. Fitting is phase-independent and per-line randomness is persistent. Keep Grids fixed.

idea: Compress the folds of a paper-like ribbon and open them again.
note: Keep Lines, preset and fold structure fixed. Large changes may cross lines; use 48 frames.

idea: Rotate the same cloud around its Y axis with Yaw.
note: Keep the file and Max points fixed. Dots or short strokes are lighter to plot; compute wire neighbours once in 3D.

idea: Let dots breathe in size while their centres stay still.
note: Keep Spacing, layout and Seed fixed. Check how Random placement depends on size; Square and Hex are clearer starting points.

idea: Rotate a solid with Rotate Y or open its faces with Explode.
note: Keep the shape fixed. Use no fill or a sparse hatch for a manageable first plot.

idea: Reveal a prepared continuous-line portrait with Carve.
note: Changing Seed, Detail or density redraws the portrait rather than animating its expression. A persistent scribble phase or landmark morph would need new support.

idea: Deform a fixed arrangement gently with Lens.
note: Proposed: closed harmonic motion around persistent centres. Changing size can rebuild the non-overlapping packing.

idea: Vary camera yaw or cable sag around a fixed structure.
note: Keep the model and anchors fixed. Check automatic fitting across the entire movement.

idea: Reveal the paths of one completed image approximation.
note: Keep the image, Count, Search, Seed and palette fixed. Re-optimising the image every frame does not preserve individual shapes.

idea: Breathe the wobble or drift of a fixed set of loops.
note: Keep Loops, Gap and Seed fixed. A noise amplitude change is not a travelling phase.

idea: Pulse ray length or wave amplitude around a stationary centre.
note: Keep the ray spacing and structure fixed. A travelling wave phase on persistent rays would be a useful extension.

idea: Grow and shrink lines in Fixed length mode.
note: Keep Count, Seed and directions fixed. Free mode uses a different construction and needs a separate continuity check.

idea: Sweep the ray angle through a small range.
note: Intersection points can jump or disappear. Inspect the whole loop before drawing a large batch.

idea: Open and close the gap around the ray centre.
note: Keep centres, placement and Seed fixed. Shared centres are easier to control than recalculating separate centroids.

idea: Explode a fixed set of rectangular pieces and return them.
note: Proposed: interpolate each persistent piece between its original and collage position. Changing Seed or Pieces creates a different arrangement.

idea: Sway the reeds with Lean and Bend.
note: Keep Count, Seed, Fallen and Broken fixed. Delayed wind motion for each stem would be a useful addition.

idea: Keep registration marks stationary throughout the series.
note: Add them after moving or cropping the artwork, with identical pen, positions and size. Remove them only in the final video crop.

idea: Breathe the throat or flare while the camera stays fixed.
note: Keep Rings and Spokes fixed. Keep Seed fixed in Laser floor mode too.

idea: Use a fixed path direction for every frame.
note: This reverses drawing order, not the visible geometry. Direction-sensitive Brush Z or Fade Out effects need consistent settings.

idea: Breathe Organic / Pleated width and folds, or vary the pockets in Channels.
note: Keep Bends, Flares, Pockets, Lines and Seed fixed. Twist is not a loop phase, so an integer change need not close a loop. A dedicated Fold phase with fixed fitting is proposed.

idea: Stretch or slant the same filament letters.
note: Keep the text and filament density fixed. Width or Gap can change path counts; delayed motion per glyph would need additional support.

idea: Pulse the strength of the water distortion.
note: A travelling Ripple phase is proposed. Keep Seed, Breakup and the waterline fixed.

idea: Let a chain of pearls swell and drift.
note: Size-dependent spacing can change the pearl count. Persistent anchors and a separate ring phase would make smoother loops.

idea: Play a cached growth sequence forwards and backwards.
note: Simulation steps are not naturally periodic. Resampling the evolving history may still introduce jumps.

idea: Reveal a fixed street map or animate a marker along a route.
note: A route-distance control is proposed. Districts, Spacing and Seed change the map itself.

idea: Sway a prepared drawing, with stronger motion in the greens.
note: A wind phase should preserve each root. Avoid rerunning placement as sizes change.

idea: Move the distortion or offset of a fixed round mask.
note: Keep Radius, Lobes and Seed fixed. Add stationary registration marks after the effect.

idea: Keep the ruler as a static measurement reference.
note: Spacing changes the ticks and numbers. Use a separate marker for a moving pointer.

idea: Reveal a fixed rune field with a moving wave.
note: A Glyph phase or Shift mode could reorder the same alphabet. Changing Seed rebuilds the text.

idea: Change density in deliberate steps.
note: Keep Lines, Grain length and Seed fixed. Probability thresholds can flicker; a periodic phase would be better for smooth movement.

idea: Move raking waves around a fixed arrangement of stones.
note: A Rake phase that preserves the stones is proposed. Concentric paths can join or split as their geometry changes.

idea: Use repeatable random values as fixed variations between objects.
note: Connecting Frame # to Seed produces a deliberate boiling effect, not smooth motion.

idea: Rotate the view around fixed scaffolding.
note: Keep Bays, Lifts, Shape and Seed fixed. Line rendering is lighter to plot than tubes.

idea: Reveal a fixed diagnostic-style drawing through a moving window.
note: An anatomical slice or pulse on one persistent specimen is proposed. Detail and Seed do not represent adjacent slices.

idea: Move and rotate a stable set of fragments.
note: Keep direction, Seed and source geometry fixed. Changing the source can change fragment identities.

idea: Breathe the messiness or legibility of the same text.
note: Keep Text, Alphabet, Loops and Seed fixed. A dedicated scribble phase could preserve the underlying strokes more reliably.

idea: Move contour halos by changing their starting level.
note: Keep Count, Step and Cell fixed. Contours can merge or split; this is an expected structural change.

idea: Keep closed-path starting points consistent across frames.
note: This changes where a stroke starts, not its visible XY position. Keep overlap fixed to avoid changing ink density at the seam.

idea: Remap an existing multicolour drawing before export.
note: Set a simple colour on the source node itself. Palette-index changes make stepped colour sequences and affect the physical pen workflow.

idea: Orbit a light using two phase-offset LFOs for its X and Y position.
note: Keep Levels and Pitch fixed. Threshold-based hatching can appear or disappear abruptly.

idea: Reveal a fixed landscape or sway the view gently.
note: Persistent landscape layers, a boat on a closed route and a water phase are proposed. Relief, Trees and Seed can rebuild the scene.

idea: Reshape time to change the easing or repeat a motion.
note: Easing cannot make incompatible end poses join. Use an integer number of repetitions for a loop.

idea: Select a wired sheet or frame using an integer control.
note: This selects existing inputs rather than evaluating time. Frame Grid is better for collecting an animation.

idea: Print Frame # + 1 outside the final image area.
note: Keep the numbering for capture and assembly. Crop it from the video to prevent a flickering signature.

idea: Reduce points with a fixed tolerance across the series.
note: Inspect corners that change adaptively. Animating the tolerance itself can cause visible jumps.

idea: Move a marker around a circle or ellipse.
note: A useful clock and alignment test. Coordinates are canvas millimetres, not a live machine position readout.

idea: Sway the horizontal and vertical skew around the canvas centre.
note: Keep the pivot fixed and avoid angles near 90°.

idea: Breathe building heights in a fixed skyline.
note: Keep Seed and the building layout fixed. Storey counts change in steps; separate layer offsets are better for smooth parallax.

idea: Slide the cursor over stationary scales.
note: Keep the scales fixed. Some markings use logarithmic rather than linear mapping.

idea: Breathe the smear length or move its zone.
note: Keep Zone mode fixed and inspect boundaries. Keep sampling consistent; zone edges can introduce abrupt changes.

idea: Sway an existing smoke form with Wind.
note: Drift is not a periodic clock. Closed noise motion on persistent filaments is proposed; keep Streams and Seed fixed.

idea: Open folds or twist a fixed filament surface.
note: Keep Sheets, Filaments and Seed fixed. Twist is not a 0–1 clock; a separate fold phase and fixed camera would help.

idea: Apply the same smoothing to every frame.
note: Keep Radius and Iterations fixed. Adaptive treatment of corners can still change the structure.

idea: Deform one prepared tangle after generation.
note: Persistent filaments with a closed coil or noise phase are proposed. Memory and Mess affect the integrated path sensitively.

idea: Sway rows of flakes with Spin and Spin variation.
note: Keep Count, branches and Seed fixed. In Scatter, zero Spin can select a different random branch; symmetry may also hide a full rotation.

idea: Rotate a solid around Y through one complete turn.
note: Keep Size, perspective and centre fixed. A cube is an inexpensive first plotting test.

idea: Move a fixed-length sampling window through the sound.
note: Keep Length fixed and avoid running off the end. Seamless one-way scrolling needs wrapped audio sampling.

idea: Breathe the pen offset while the gear system stays fixed.
note: Keep R, r and Turns fixed. Changing tooth counts changes the curve's period and structure.

idea: Give fixed branches different transformations.
note: Keep the output count fixed. Use Frame Grid to collect different moments in time.

idea: Separate a fixed palette into physical pen passes.
note: Preview selection is not an animation control. Preserve pen identities and registration across all frames.

idea: Breathe the central hole or swirl of a gill print.
note: Keep Primary gills, Gap, Seed and detail fixed. Intermediate branching may still change in steps.

idea: Breathe the squiggle amplitude.
note: Keep Period and Mode fixed. Travelling motion would require a Phase control.

idea: Rotate or scale repeated motifs locally along a path.
note: Keep Spacing and Seed fixed. Orientation is relative to the supporting path.

idea: Rotate a fixed chart or reveal its marks.
note: Keep Hits, Rings and Seed fixed. An Observation phase is proposed; dense point fields can be expensive to plot.

idea: Rotate the view of a fixed 3D star field.
note: Closed parallax or twinkling with persistent stars would be useful additions. Count and Seed determine star identities.

idea: Select regions in deliberate steps.
note: For example, show six regions over 24 frames. This makes hard cuts; use a moving Container for a smoother reveal.

idea: Quantise a clock into a fixed number of states.
note: Choose a step count that divides 24 or 48 and use phase i/N. This is useful for switches and deliberate jumps.

idea: Reveal or deform one completed stipple drawing.
note: Changing Gamma can repack points. Frozen centres with animated dot size or fill would preserve the drawing better.

idea: Breathe the pixel size of stitched letters.
note: Keep font, Cell, text and motif fixed. Check whether halo randomness or counts change.

idea: Deform a fixed stone arrangement gently with Lens.
note: Persistent stones with moving light or shadow are proposed. Changing size can rebuild non-overlapping packing.

idea: Stretch a selected band and let it return.
note: Keep the band and pivot fixed. Leave room for the tail and crop only after the deformation.

idea: Rotate stripes inside stationary circles.
note: Keep stripe spacing fixed. Check small angle steps at 24 frames for moiré aliasing.

idea: Move a signal or reveal a route on a fixed map.
note: A route phase with station stops is proposed. Lines, Grid and Seed change the map rather than moving a train.

idea: Morph gently between flower and star-like outlines.
note: Keep m and Rings fixed; vary n1, n2 and n3 within moderate positive ranges to avoid extreme spikes.

idea: Animate transformations of the same imported SVG.
note: Keep the file and pen mapping fixed. Fonts and CSS do not automatically become plotter paths.

idea: Advance Phase through 360° in Circle or Helix mode.
note: This rotates the route rather than moving a profile along its tail. Line mode is unaffected; keep Instances low and fixed.

idea: Switch between inputs on an integer clock.
note: Use Steps for deliberate cuts. This is not a morph; continuous Morph Layers support is a separate proposal.

idea: Move a symmetry centre while keeping the fold count fixed.
note: Animating the source before copying it is another useful way to preserve a stable repeated structure.

idea: Breathe the deformation strength around a fixed zone.
note: Keep Seed and Scale fixed. Moving the affected region can cause abrupt boundary changes.

idea: Print one calibration card before the animation batch.
note: Check line width, hatching and lifts. Do not repeat the full card in every frame; measured drawing time is more useful than a guess.

idea: Advance Start % along a closed path.
note: Use Align Start. Centre alignment can reset the offset; letters may bunch at the end of an open path. Keep text and tracking fixed.

idea: Turn tiles or vary the superellipse exponent in a fixed grid.
note: Keep Rows, Columns, Shape and Seed fixed. Super N only affects Superellipse mode.

idea: Change tile order in a deliberate stepped sequence.
note: Amount selects a permutation rather than a continuous path. Interpolated tile routes with collision handling and a closed return are proposed.

idea: Turn a drawing around a polar centre with Start angle.
note: Use 0–360° and keep Turns and Inner radius fixed. Many turns can accumulate ink near the centre.

idea: Open and close the gap in a fixed torn form.
note: Keep Fling, Snap, Detail and Seed fixed. Boundaries can change discretely; begin with a small Gape range.

idea: Use Image → Contours for the legacy tracing workflow.
note: This hidden compatibility alias is not a separate animation tool. Keep the image and sampling grid fixed.

idea: Optimise the route of each frame for production.
note: Use Show direction to inspect it. Travel Sort does not affect SVG or DXF exports and is not a visible animation effect.

idea: Add production pauses where the plotting workflow needs them.
note: These pauses control the machine workflow, not the animated image.

idea: Grow or shorten the ends of existing strokes.
note: Short paths may disappear. This can work well with hairs, arrows and other repeated marks.

idea: Breathe tile scale or rounding in a fixed pattern.
note: Keep Tile, Seed, Fill and Mode fixed. Loop mode describes a geometric pattern, not an animation clock.

idea: Deform one fixed subdivided tile pattern.
note: Persistent subdivision and a tile-turn phase are proposed. Changing Seed changes the structure.

idea: Sway tree trunks with Lean.
note: Keep Count, Width and Seed fixed. A wind phase that increases towards the crown would be a useful addition.

idea: Rotate or change the radius of a fixed tube bundle.
note: Keep Count, Seed, Surface and Density fixed. Drift is not periodic time; hidden-line visibility changes with the view.

idea: Rotate the drawing through a full turn with Start angle.
note: Keep the program and Seed fixed and check automatic fitting. The text program is not a numeric animation input.

idea: Vary density in deliberate steps on a fixed grid.
note: A repeatable sequence of seeds makes intentional noise boiling. A moving Band phase is proposed for smoother motion.

idea: Shift or slant the type beneath a fixed grating.
note: Keep Pitch and Mode fixed. Interference and clipping are part of the effect; a separate raster phase would help.

idea: Reveal a fixed text field through a moving window.
note: Row and Column phase controls could wrap the same letters through a fixed grid. Density and Seed do not make a continuous falling motion.

idea: Apply one shared style to moving paths.
note: An animated Stroke phase can affect the drawing, but may create additional paths and pen lifts.

idea: Use a static calibration pattern or deform it as artwork.
note: Keep calibration areas fixed. Zone plates can alias in both physical plotting and video capture.

idea: Rotate a flat drawing or relief with Yaw and Roll.
note: Keep bounds and perspective fixed. Avoid singular views; an edge-on drawing can legitimately disappear.

idea: Move a dashed style through one dash-plus-gap period.
note: For dashes the period is in millimetres, not automatically 0–1. Set jitter and variation to zero; check the period of other styles separately.

idea: Use a fixed chart as a graphic source.
note: Do not treat an animation as an acuity test. Persistent dots would be needed for a stable pseudoiso animation.

idea: Breathe the height or dip of a fixed volcanic surface.
note: Keep Render, Spacing, flutes and Seed fixed. Inspect hidden-line changes over 48 frames.

idea: Deform a fixed Voronoi diagram with Lens or Cage.
note: Persistent site identities moving on closed routes are proposed. Cells and Seed create a new diagram.

idea: Move the corners while preserving their order and a convex outline.
note: Avoid a collapsed or crossed quadrilateral. For a grid warp, breathe amplitude with Seed fixed.

idea: Breathe the wave amplitude of a fixed water field.
note: Periodic Wave phase or closed noise motion is proposed. Keep Lines, Wavelength, Choppiness and Seed fixed.

idea: Breathe amplitude or lean in a fixed hatch field.
note: A shared travelling Phase is proposed. Keep Band, Pitch and Seed fixed; path counts may still change.

idea: Change heading or tilt gently.
note: A Tail or Flipper phase, and delayed tentacle motion for the octopus, would add internal movement. Keep species, count and Seed fixed.

idea: Sweep the wind angle through a small range.
note: Keep Lines fixed. Flow separation may change routes; moving markers along fixed streamlines would be more stable.

idea: Breathe eccentricity or wobble in a fixed grain pattern.
note: Keep Rings, Cracks and Seed fixed. A grain phase or eccentricity angle is proposed.

idea: Deform a prepared worm after generation.
note: A gait phase with delayed feet on a persistent spine is proposed. Wander and Seed rebuild the shape.

idea: Open spacing or splits in a fixed woven route.
note: Keep Grid, Steps and Seed fixed. A travelling weave phase should preserve the route rather than generate new random turns.

idea: Breathe raking-wave amplitude around fixed stones.
note: Keep stones, rings and spacing fixed. A dedicated Rake phase is proposed.

idea: Vary the existing phase to move different rows by different amounts.
note: Phase 0–1 is multiplied by row index, leaving the first row stationary. It is not a global phase; that would need a separate control.

idea: Run Phase from 0 to 1 for one wave cycle.
note: For a closed path, use a whole number of wavelengths. Keep Wavelength and Seed fixed. Sine gives smooth motion; Coil can change the path count.

idea: Arrange a 24–48-frame flipbook as a separate folding project.
note: This does not automatically evaluate the timeline. Collect the frames with Frame Grid first.

idea: Package a shared clock and movement controls as a reusable group.
note: Promote clear control names and keep one shared clock. Nested frame evaluation cannot be stacked without checking its context.

idea: Use Travel Sort or the export optimiser for current routing workflows.
note: This hidden legacy routing node is not an image animation effect.
